---
title: "Starting point or expectations are unclear"
last-reviewed: "2026-08-28"
---

## Find the missing expectation

If an instruction such as “develop the proposal” leaves you unsure where to start, ask what the next version needs to show. University requirements, a supervisor's preferences and your own assumptions can easily get mixed together.

## Try this now

1. Check the current candidature milestone or written task.
2. Look at an accepted example to see the level of detail expected.
3. Note what you think your version needs to show and ask the reviewer to confirm anything unclear.
4. Record what you'll produce, by when, who will review it and how you'll know it's ready.

## What to take when asking

Try: “I think this version needs to show [outcome]. I've checked [requirement/example], but I'm unsure about [point]. I propose sending [draft or other work] by [date]. Would that give you what you need to review?”

## Route

- Expectations differ between supervisors: use the [supervisor expectations guide](../templates/supervisor-expectations.qmd).
- The task is too large: convert it into a milestone and next action.
- No one can identify the authority: ask the graduate research coordinator or responsible office.

## Stop or escalate

Escalate repeated non-response, irreconcilable instructions, unsafe expectations or formal milestones threatened by missing direction.

## You are moving again when

You and the reviewer agree on the next piece of work, the standard it needs to meet and the date.
